{{@ class $highlightText}}TOP SECRET{{/}}{{titleParagraph}}{{@ class $highlightText}}SECTOR: N-07 ("Aurora" Perimeter){{/}}{{pargraphStart}}Our prediction was correct. Station observers recorded the anomaly's approach 11 days prior to the event. For the first time, we saw it coming.{{pargraphStart}}During the calm before the storm, production of ATLAS complexes was standardized. New modules are assembled faster and calibrated more precisely. We carried out training, ran through formations, and prepared back-up squads. Full alert.{{pargraphStart}}But the anomaly had its own plans.{{pargraphStart}}The Funnel didn't open in the predicted sector. It appeared here, in a remote northern region, far from the deployed infrastructure. It's not clear why this location was chosen. Nothing in the models had indicated this area. Emergency redeployment was initiated immediately, but the terrain and distance aren't in our favor. Some vehicles and squads will arrive late.{{pargraphStart}}Every ATLAS complex we managed to deliver is now indispensable.{{pargraphStart}}This time, we were ready for combat. But for combat in a different location.{{pargraphStart}}SIGNATURE: CURATOR (PROJECT M)

{{@ class $highlightText}}Analytical Memo 27/C "INVASION LOCATION SELECTION"{{/}}{{titleParagraph}}For internal use. "Restricted Access" stamp.{{pargraphStart}}I ask a question I'm obliged to answer, but can't: Why here?{{pargraphStart}}This region has no strategic value for the Funnel. There's nothing here. No infrastructure, no settlements. Only a non-operational military base on the island. Echo tanks can't cross the sea. So why capture a location they can't attack from? {{pargraphStart}}I requested the region's full operational history. The reply was heavily redacted. Whole sections had been blanked out. A second request was sent back with the note "access restricted by the authority of {{@ class $highlightSecondaryText}}[DATA REMOVED]{{/}}." I, the head of the research department, whose recommendations determine this sector's defense strategy, am being denied information about this territory!{{pargraphStart}}Here's what I can deduce from field data: the Funnel's behavior doesn't correspond to what we observed in sector R-22. New types of echo tanks that we haven't encountered before have appeared. They correspond in function to our long-range tank destroyers and are extremely effective on this kind of terrain. The opponent has learned from our tactics and taken countermeasures. Now it's our turn to adapt.{{pargraphStart}}It might be that it needs this place. Or maybe what's underneath it.{{pargraphStart}}I don't know. And it worries me that somebody knows, but won't say.{{pargraphStart}}SIGNATURE: CURATOR (PROJECT M)

{{@ class $highlightText}}CURATOR'S PERSONAL RECORD{{/}}{{pargraphStart}}I've reviewed my own hypotheses. All three.{{pargraphStart}}  1. The anomaly seeks to destroy us. {{pargraphStart}}  2. The anomaly is experimenting. It researches our tactics, studies our response, adjusts, and learns.{{pargraphStart}}  3. The anomaly is training. Each wave is a drill of its new tactics; each battle is training in field conditions.{{pargraphStart}}All three hypotheses share the assumption that we are the target of this invasion.{{pargraphStart}}But what if we aren't?{{pargraphStart}}What if the anomaly is doing something else, and we're simply standing in its way? Like an ant nest flooded while a road's being built. The builder doesn't wage war with the ants. It simply doesn't notice them.{{pargraphStart}}You can stop an enemy who wants to destroy you. You can negotiate with them. But you can't scare something that doesn't acknowledge your existence; you can't outsmart it. It can't be stopped. Because you were never part of its calculations.{{pargraphStart}}I think we've been asking the wrong question. We shouldn't be asking why it's attacking us, but whether it notices us at all.{{pargraphStart}}SIGNATURE: CURATOR (PROJECT M)

{{@ class $highlightText}}FINAL REPORT{{/}}{{titleParagraph}}{{@ class $highlightText}}STATUS: DECLASSIFIED (PARTLY){{/}}{{pargraphStart}}At 03:47, the Funnel collapsed. The anomaly's activity stopped. The sector is clear.{{pargraphStart}}In the final seconds before the collapse, ATLAS meters registered an energy surge that exceeded all previously recorded values. The crews observed a short-lived physical manifestation in the center of the anomaly, which lasted no longer than 12 seconds. After that, the Funnel closed. {{pargraphStart}}Official statement: The incident is over. The territory has been successfully defended. The quarantine has been lifted from the sector.{{pargraphStart}}{{@ class $highlightText}}CURATOR'S PERSONAL NOTE (Only for special reserves){{/}}{{pargraphStart}}We didn't win. It finished.{{pargraphStart}}This wasn't an invasion. It was a cover. A protective perimeter around what manifested in the Funnel's center seconds before its collapse.{{pargraphStart}}Dozens of Obelisks appeared simultaneously. We still don't know what they were doing. ATLAS recorded all the parameters, but it will take time to interpret them. We know one thing with near certainty: the anomaly completed some kind of process.{{pargraphStart}}Whatever it was doing, we need to prepare for the next attack. We have enough data now. Our engineers are already going through the recordings, and, to be honest, I've never seen them so excited. They think we can seriously strengthen our vehicles. We need to do so before the Funnel returns. {{pargraphStart}}I can't stop thinking about one thing: if this happened here and lasted such a short time, how many times has it happened before? In places where there was no ATLAS, no one to see it happening...{{pargraphStart}}SIGNATURE: CURATOR (PROJECT M)
